evidence_class: Mocked: fakeredis command queue, operation journal and execution registry, a fake server clock, a fixture network between worker and API, and an in process run of the worker helper standing in for kubectl exec; no Kubernetes API server, kubelet exec or live worker Pod was used.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.commands: KubernetesCommandTransport(queue, pods, runner, expires_in_ms, fallback_enabled) is the runtime CommandTransport for backend kubernetes carrying answer, drain and cancel; apply_operation issues the structured command into the SV2-LDG-05 CommandQueue keyed by the operation id with the execution generation and expiry, and the worker receives it over the authenticated command endpoint

observe_operation reconciles by the command id derived from the operation id: a stored command that matches the operation's execution, generation and payload digest is applied, a missing one is absent and may be issued again because issuing is idempotent per key, any mismatch is refused, an unavailable store is unknown

fallback(execution_id, command_id) delivers only an issued, unexpired command, only when the fallback is enabled, and only into the Pod swarm-<execution_id> in the client namespace carrying this swarm's owner label and the command's execution and generation labels; it runs the fixed helper argv python -m scripts.swarm_v2.worker.control with one mode and one argument, asks status first and delivers only on absent
KubectlExec runs kubectl exec --namespace --container agent -- with an argv list and no shell; a timeout raises TimeoutError and a missing kubectl ConnectionError

sanitize_report removes escape and control sequences other than newline and tab, replaces invalid UTF-8, redacts secrets with the strict hooks.secrets patterns and bounds each report to 2048 characters before helper stdout and stderr are stored in worker-transport-reports
worker_transport_ambiguous_total(store, slug) counts helper calls per mode (status, deliver) whose reply was lost or did not match its exit code and command id

scripts.swarm_v2.worker.control: encode and decode carry the command id, execution id, generation, kind, payload, payload digest and expiry as one URL safe base64 JSON argument; decode refuses wrong fields, a malformed command id, non integer generation or expiry and a payload digest mismatch

main(argv) is the only helper a controller may exec: deliver ENVELOPE queues an envelope for this Pod's launch execution and generation before its expiry into the worker inbox with an exclusive link, status COMMAND_ID answers queued, known or absent; anything else is refused with exit 2 and one JSON line

WorkerControl(transport, state_path, handlers, inbox) takes inbox envelopes like polled commands and still acknowledges them over the authenticated endpoint before running them, so the fallback never bypasses server acceptance, expiry or the run once rule
scripts.swarm_v2.api.commands: CommandQueue.command_id(execution_id, key) names the id issue uses

supported_versions.kubernetes: kubectl exec into the agent container of an SV2-KUB-01 execution Pod; exercised only through the in process helper, no live release
supported_versions.redis: the SV2-LDG-05 worker command queue and the SV2-RUN-04 operation journal; commands issued before this package are read unchanged
supported_versions.compatibility: The local runtime, its command transports and the worker command endpoint are unchanged; the worker command and runtime command test modules pass with this branch (proofs run 38071968276). The transport registers only under backend kubernetes.

authority: The actor comes from Commands, which accepts only an authenticated operator or the current master incarnation, and the command queue issues only to the current occupant generation of the seat; a forged credential is refused before any write in case B. The fallback execs only into a Pod whose owner label is owner_for(slug) and whose execution and generation labels match the stored command; the helper refuses an envelope for another execution or generation of its own launch record. Kubernetes RBAC for pods/exec in the worker namespace bounds who can run the helper at all.
authoritative_objects: The worker command queue in Redis and the runtime operation journal are authoritative; the worker state file holds the worker's own run record. Helper reports, the ambiguity counts and the inbox files are observational or transient and may be dropped.

states.observed: Cases A, B and C each ran twice with identical records in proofs runs 38071839436 and 38071968276.
states.accepted: Answers from the fixture reach the worker handler with the exact structured payload over HTTP and over the fallback helper, and a drain puts the worker in no new mutations mode and completes on its checkpoint. Shell metacharacters stay message content and every helper argv is the fixed helper plus a mode and a URL safe argument. A lost delivery reply is reconciled by command id with a status probe and never delivered twice, and a lost issue reply is reconciled by command id without a second issue.
states.committed: Code and fixture inputs are at tested_commit; manifest.json hashes them.
states.externally_verified: None: no live API server, exec or G3 deployment was exercised.

validation.red: proofs run 38071702796 on the tests only commit f78dc848: collection of the Kubernetes command tests fails on the missing module and every new worker control test fails on the missing helper functions
validation.tests: proofs run 38071968276 at 487ae7d4: 253 passed across the Kubernetes commands, worker control, worker commands, runtime commands and Kubernetes runtime modules; only the then absent case A, manifest and result records failed
validation.lint: ruff check and ruff format passed through python -m scripts.ci_prepush

rollback_rehearsal.action: Construct or switch the transport with fallback_enabled False: fallback answers disabled without reading the Pod or running exec, while apply_operation keeps issuing commands that the worker receives over the authenticated endpoint.
rollback_rehearsal.proof: Case B ends with the fallback disabled: the next answer is delivered over HTTP and the helper is not called.

remaining_limitations: The worker loop in the image does not yet construct WorkerControl with the helper inbox and state paths; the helper writes into /home/worker/commands, which the supervisor must wire when the worker command loop lands.
The fallback only delivers: acknowledgement and completion still need the authenticated endpoint, so a worker that cannot reach the controller holds a fallback command as received until it expires.
The Pod name is derived from the execution id by the SV2-KUB-01 naming rule rather than read from the execution registry, whose runtime target still carries a placeholder.
Helper reports and ambiguity counts are kept in Redis per swarm and not exported as telemetry yet.
The controller host needs kubectl and a pods/exec grant for the fallback; neither ships with this package.
